rows.requirement: BIGTREETECH TMC2209 V1.3 removable modules, heatsinks, two R110 current-sense resistors per module (qty 6)
rows.title: BIGTREETECH TMC2209 V1.3 Stepper Motor Driver, 2.8A Ultra Silent Stepsticks
rows.evidence: Listing text: V1.3; pack of 6 drivers plus heatsinks; TMC2209-LA; VIO 3-5 V; VM 4.75-28 V; UART is the default mode. VERIFIED-FROM-SOURCE (BTT GitHub bigtreetech/BIGTREETECH-Stepper-Motor-Driver, TMC2209/V1.3/Schematic/TMC2209 V1.3-SCH.pdf): sense resistors R3 and R5 = 0R11 on BRA/BRB (R110); header P1A pin 1 DIR, 2 STEP, 3 CLK (20k pull-down), 4 UART_TX, 5 UART_RX (= IC pin 14 PDN_UART), 6 MS2, 7 MS1, 8 EN; 9 VS (VM), 10 GND, 11 A2, 12 A1, 13 B1, 14 B2, 15 VIO, 16 GND; P1B pins 17 INDEX, 18 DIAG, 19 VREF; R10 bridge UART_TX-UART_RX marked NC. In A4988 position terms: EN, MS1, MS2, MS3=PDN_UART, RST=UART_TX (not connected), SLP=CLK, STEP, DIR / VMOT, GND, 2B=A2, 2A=A1, 1A=B1, 1B=B2, VDD=VIO, GND. BTT V1.3 manual: UART is default; to move UART, bridge R10. IMAGE-ONLY (Amazon alt text, unverified): a 'UART Mode' panel shows the factory-default PDN_UART pin and the solder option; V1.3 adds an ESD diode and capacitor vs V1.2.
rows.gaps: Listing text never states R110 or the pin order (those come from BTT's schematic). Inspect received boards: sense resistors printed R110 and silkscreen matching the schematic before socket insertion. BTT V1.3 manual lists VM 12-28 V; listing says 4.75-28 V.

rows.requirement: STEPstick carrier with separate VM, GND, VIO, STEP, DIR, EN, MS1, MS2 and accessible PDN_UART; >=35 V electrolytic at VM (qty 6)
rows.title: 10 Pcs 5x7CM FR4 Double Side Prototype PCB Tinned Universal Breadboard
rows.evidence: NO PRIME CARRIER PRODUCT MEETS THIS ROW. Recommended: build six carriers on these 0.1-inch double-sided proto boards with two 1x8 female headers each (driver_carriers__female_headers) placed 5 holes (12.7 mm) apart, one Rubycon 100 uF 50 V (capacitors row) across VM/GND at the socket, and every module pin brought out by name: VM, GND, VIO, EN, STEP, DIR, MS1, MS2, PDN_UART (the MS3-position pin), with CLK tied to GND or left on its module pull-down and the RST-position pin (UART_TX) left unconnected. Exposure of PDN_UART and MS1/MS2 is verified by construction.
rows.gaps: Requires soldering and hand labelling (X/Y/Z/U/V/W, EN corner, pin-1 mark). 180-degree insertion of a 2x8 module puts VM on DIR and GND on STEP; mark the EN/VM end. Derek's on-hand 2-pin 2.54 mm screw terminals (x20) and 3-pin 5.08 mm pluggable terminals (x10) can carry VM/GND; signal leads otherwise solder to pads.

rows.requirement: FoMaKo K20UH 4K PTZ camera with USB 3.0 4K output, x2 (two complementary views of dot, wire tip and seam)
rows.title: FoMaKo 4K HDMI PTZ Camera NDI AI Auto-Tracking(Gen 3), NDI HX3 Certified, 20X Optical Zoom, USB 3.0 LAN HDMI PTZ Camera 4K ... (NDI License Included), K20UH
rows.evidence: Listing: 4K30 (3840x2160) HDMI/LAN/USB 3.0, 1/2.8in CMOS 8.42MP, 20x optical, pan +/-170 deg, tilt -30..+90 deg, 'PoE supported' (bullets and brand comparison chart), VISCA over IP, NDI HX3. Manual (https://www.fomako.net/uploads/20250529/ce40713967c8ae0e137cabdd8a72ff1d.pdf): USB 3.0 MJPG/H.264 up to 3840x2160@30 (YUY2/NV12 max 1080p30) in 'USB 4K mode', and USB outputs 4K only when the HDMI output format is set to 4K; in USB 4K mode LAN main stream and NDI are limited to 1080p30. Network port 10/100BASE-TX (100 Mbps). VISCA ports 1259 (IP VISCA) and 52381 (Sony VISCA); web login admin/admin; DHCP on by default, falls back to 192.168.5.163 if no router assigns an address. Power: DC 12V +/-10%, max 1 A / 12 W, 'HEC3800 outlet (DC12V)'; adapter AC 110-220 V in, DC 12 V 2.0 A out. LAN 'POE&NDI optional, consult dealer for specific models'. Body 253.5 x 144 x 169 mm, 1.46 kg. Rear panel (Figure 1.1 drawing): USB 3.0 Standard-B receptacle, HDMI, 3.5 mm line-in, 5-pin RS232/RS485 Phoenix, RJ45 LAN, DC12V jack, power switch. Base (Figure 1.1 bottom view): one 'screw hole for tripod' centred in a mounting plate with three 'holes for installation fixation'; four round pads at the corners. Power-on self-test: pans left, returns to centre, zoom runs to tele then back to wide, then goes to preset 0 if saved. Manual install rules: stable horizontal surface, not mounted obliquely (gravity sensor supports inverted auto-flip), no obstacles within the pan/tilt range, never turn the head/lens by hand (can cause self-check failure), do not power on before installation is complete. Reviews on this ASIN (Classic Black): base has a 1/4in tripod thread (reviewer); one reviewer powers it over PoE (Mar 2026).
gaps: PoE: listing says supported and a K20UH reviewer runs it on PoE, but the manual calls PoE model-dependent and no PoE standard/class is stated (12 W max draw fits 802.3af). Not assumed: the included 12 V adapters are the baseline; a PoE+ switch is the switch row's alternate.
Included USB cable is USB-A to USB-B (reviewer) of unstated length, reported too short; the Mac host has only USB-C ports, so row 4 sources 2 m USB-C to USB-B 3.0 cables.
USB connector type comes from the manual's rear-panel drawing (USB 3.0 Standard-B); the manual text and listing only say 'USB 3.0'.
DC plug dimensions not stated (manual: 'HEC3800 outlet'); adapter DC lead 1.5 m per reviewer, so each PSU must sit within ~1.5 m of its camera or be extended.
4K over USB needs 'USB 4K mode' with the HDMI output format set to 4K; NDI/LAN are then 1080p30. Settings must be fixed and recorded per the study.

Ethernet is 100 Mbps only. On an isolated switch (no DHCP) both cameras fall back to 192.168.5.163: assign static IPs one camera at a time via the web page (Mac Ethernet set manually to 192.168.5.x), or provide DHCP. FoMaKo's IP Scanner tool is Windows-only; Mac users in reviews reported network-control setup friction.

Tripod socket: 1/4in thread per reviewer only; thread DEPTH not stated in manual text/drawings, fomako.net product page/FAQ, or listing. Unverified - measure before first fit (see screw row). Thread size of the three fixation holes is also unstated.
Power-on self-test pans the head and drives the zoom through its range, so the DCR-250 stage must be retracted clear of the head's sweep before any power-up or reboot (including PoE switch restarts).
Listing vs manual box contents differ (mounts listed as included vs optional; RS232 cable omitted from listing); reviewer units contained both. IR remote needs 2x AAA (not supplied).
Warranty wording on the listing is inconsistent (1-year in bullets, 3-year in details).
Simultaneous capture of two 3840x2160 MJPG streams on the host Mac (MacBook Air M3) is untested.

gaps: Why needed: the host observed in this session is a MacBook Air M3 (Mac15,12) with two Thunderbolt/USB4 ports, each its own bus/xHCI, and no wired Ethernet. One port carries a CH340 USB-serial adapter, the other a 5 Gbps Anker hub with the 16MP USB 2.0 overview camera.

Proposed topology: Mac port A -> camera A directly (USB-C to USB-B); Mac port B -> this hub -> camera B (USB-C to USB-B into the hub's USB-C data port), overview camera, CH340, and Gigabit Ethernet -> switch uplink. Each 4K camera then sits on its own Thunderbolt bus.

Powered USB 3 hub: not required for power - the K20UH is self-powered (12 V/PoE) and the other hub devices are low-draw; the real constraints are port count and keeping the two 4K streams on separate buses. Untested: two simultaneous 3840x2160 MJPG streams on the M3 Air.
Exact USB-A/USB-C split of the 4 data ports is image-only, unverified.

No-hub alternative: uplink the switch to the house router and reach the cameras over the Mac's Wi-Fi (no purchase, adds router/Wi-Fi dependency). Or, if the existing Anker hub has a free port, a plain USB Ethernet adapter on it would also work (not sourced).

The manual's bottom view shows four round corner pads (likely rubber feet). Anti-rotation/registration: the base also has three fixation holes of unstated thread (used by the included bracket/slide mount); a single 1/4in screw alone does not stop rotation.
